prize_parts.citation: for introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and thereby changing the understanding of who exports, how trade reallocates resources across firms, and the gains from trade

statement.case_for: I am moving my preferred part from B043 to B012. In round 1 I called B043 my first choice by a narrow margin and said B012 would be at least as defensible if breadth of confirmed empirical use were weighted more heavily. After the exchange I weight it that way. Melitz (2003) turned trade theory from representative industries to heterogeneous firms. Selection into exporting, reallocation toward more productive firms and a new channel for gains from trade follow directly from that step. Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) extended it to the choice between exporting and foreign direct investment, and Helpman's wider trade agenda made it a research programme. The mechanism has been tested for two decades on firm-level and transaction-level data, which is the kind of evidence I know best from my own work on pricing, invoicing and cross-border trade. Exporter premia, selection and the exporter-versus-FDI choice are visible in the micro data. The framework also reaches productivity measurement, quantitative policy evaluation and macro work on reallocation. A two-name prize avoids hard exclusions among the credited names. Trade has not been recognised since 2008, but that is a timing consideration and I do not count it as merit. My case rests on originality, breadth of confirmation and attributable credit. B043 remains a clean and original mechanism, but its evidence base rests largely on one theoretical paper, and its empirical identification is debated. Colleagues who judge B043 and B012 differently from me are making a judgement on exactly those points. I do not read the three explicit B012 supporters as scientific evidence in itself.
statement.case_against: Credit for the heterogeneous-firm agenda is wider than the pair. Bernard and Jensen documented the exporter facts, Eaton and Kortum built a closely related framework, and Redding's quantitative and spatial work is substantial. Any two-name citation must be written so it does not claim more than the originating mechanism. The welfare conclusions are also model-dependent. Pareto productivity distributions and functional-form choices matter for the quantitative gains from trade. My understanding is that some quantitative-trade work finds that welfare formulas can be less sensitive to the heterogeneity margin than the original theory suggested. I have not independently verified that, and the Committee should address it in the Scientific Background. Helpman also appears on B007, so the Committee must choose which body of his work to honour. Finally, my own field is adjacent to trade and industrial organisation, so I may over-read how persuasive the firm-level micro evidence is compared with the people-and-places evidence in B022.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B012 first with Melitz and Helpman only. He treats Redding's quantitative and spatial work as extensions of an already well-defined core, flags Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum as an attribution risk, and prefers a citation built on firm selection and reallocation to adding a third name.
responses.response: I now agree with his preferred configuration, and I move toward it from B043. I particularly agree that the omitted contributors are a drafting problem for the citation and not a reason to widen the prize. A citation that names selection and reallocation as the core mechanism credits the originating insight without claiming the empirical exporter-premia facts or the parallel Eaton-Kortum framework. Where I would press him is on how much weight to put on the welfare results. Their quantitative size depends on distributional assumptions, so the citation should rest on the mechanism and its microdata confirmation, not on a specific gains-from-trade magnitude.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B012 first, now prefers the Kiyotaki-Moore pair for B043 without Gertler, and keeps B012 ahead because the firm-heterogeneity discovery has a more extensive record of direct microdata confirmation, while collateral-driven amplification remains debated.
responses.response: His comparison persuades me, and I have changed my ordering because of it. We agree on the pair for B043 and on the weakness he names, which is how thinly and indirectly collateral-driven amplification is identified in the data. That is the point that moved me. I still think B043 has the cleaner single-paper attribution and a distinct real-side channel from the 2022 prize. But a prize committee can weigh a confirmed, widely used microfoundation above a cleanly attributed mechanism whose empirical support is more contested. I keep B043 as my first alternative, so that if colleagues weigh macro-finance more than I now do, I can support it.

responses.point: Hassler, the chair, moved from B021 to B012 on attribution grounds. He lists B043 as an alternative but cites thematic proximity to the 2022 prize and debated empirical identification, and he says a Grossman-Helpman prize should not outrank Melitz-Helpman.
responses.response: I agree with his assessment that B043's marginal novelty is lower after 2022, though I still regard collateral-constraint amplification as a distinct mechanism from bank runs and the empirical study of crises. I would treat that as a judgement the Committee should make explicitly, not a settled point. On B007, I rated it fourth and keep it out of my configuration. Helpman is better honoured once, through the broader and better-confirmed firm-heterogeneity work. I note that he and I share an IJIO co-authorship (2026) with Tore Ellingsen. I do not think that is why we converge, since my move follows from my own round-1 statement that breadth of confirmation could tip the balance.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B022 first with the Autor-Hanson-Dorn trio. He says B012 and B022 cover different ground, with B012 the more direct route to a trade prize, and he rates B022 higher for its credible designs on a question about people and places that trade theory does not address.
responses.response: I accept that the two do not substitute for each other, and the China-shock designs are credible. That is why I now list B022 among my alternatives, and it was not in my round-1 list. Where I differ is on the common-criteria weighting. The labour-market adjustment finding is robust in direction, but the size and persistence of the effects are still under re-analysis, and the task framework's credit extends beyond the named trio. The firm-heterogeneity mechanism has been confirmed on microdata with less revision to its core insight. I cannot settle explanatory reach from the supplied evidence, and I would not oppose B022 if the Committee judges societal consequence more heavily than I do.

responses.point: Andersson answered my round-1 B007 ranking and now treats B007 as an alternative, not his lead. He keeps it for its high conceptual originality and unambiguous credit, while accepting that the lobbying model's empirical predictions have mixed support.
responses.response: I agree that the Grossman-Helpman attribution is unusually clean and that the conceptual originality is high. That is why I ranked it fourth. The mixed empirical record and the narrower scope keep it behind B012 for me, and Helpman cannot sensibly be named twice. If the Committee finds firm heterogeneity too contested on attribution, B007 is a coherent fallback. I would not combine them.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee will accept a citation resting on the selection-and-reallocation mechanism despite the parallel contributions of Bernard and Jensen and of Eaton and Kortum, who are outside the ballot.
Whether adding Redding would strengthen or dilute a clean pair, and how robust the welfare conclusions are to functional-form assumptions.

Whether B043's collateral-constraint mechanism is distinct enough from the 2022 prize and the Gertler accelerator strand to take precedence over B012. My ordering of B012 over B043 is a narrow judgement, not a decisive one.
Whether the B022 plurality should outweigh my preference because I weight breadth of microdata confirmation more than societal consequence. I cannot settle that from the supplied evidence.
My recollection of credit shares and of the quantitative-trade welfare literature comes from general knowledge and has not been independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: I co-authored a 2026 IJIO paper with committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen. The chair is also a B012 supporter, so I note that the overlap exists and that my move follows from my own round-1 condition. I am married to Magdalena Andersson, a public fact in my profile. I have not linked this to any committee colleague or candidate. No collaboration with Melitz or Helpman appears in my profile, and none appears with the credited names on my alternatives B043 and B022. My research fields (industrial organisation, exchange-rate pass-through, price setting and trade) are adjacent to B012 and B029. I treat that as expertise and not as evidence of merit. I have not adjudicated these connections.
